h: A Few Pointers and a Taste of the Dear Green Place
p: Glasgow's nickname is the Dear Green Place, and it's well earned, with parks all over the city. But when the rain sets in, a trampoline park is the hero of the hour. Make your visit easier by booking ahead, filling in the online waiver before you arrive and making sure everyone has had a light snack rather than a huge lunch.

Keep valuables out of your pockets and use a locker if one is available. Grip socks can usually be kept for repeat visits, so don't throw them away. Remind the kids to stick to one per trampoline and to listen to the staff, who are there to keep everyone safe and having fun.

Once the session's over, Glasgow has some cracking free attractions to explore. Glasgow Green, by the Clyde, is a big, historic park for a leg-stretch, with the ornate Doulton Fountain as its showpiece. Glasgow Cathedral is a stunning medieval building, and just behind it, the Necropolis is a striking Victorian cemetery on a hill with fantastic views across the city.

The Burrell Collection in Pollok Country Park is another highlight, with an incredible range of art and objects in a parkland setting. Getting around is easy on the Glasgow Subway, a little circular line locals affectionately call the Clockwork Orange. It loops round the centre and the West End, so hopping between the museums, Byres Road and the city centre is quick and easy.
